ledger.claim: All three core artifacts describe the same trip, so the rider's initial burden of showing the evidence is about this trip is discharged under POL-RD-08(a): the trip record, the GPS trace and the fare breakdown each carry trip_id TRP-09112 and the same 2026-09-19 window (requested 14:02, started 14:10, ended 14:32, charged 14:32:03).

On the distance measurement there is no conflict to resolve: the GPS trace, which governs the threshold test under POL-RD-01, records 11.5 km against a booked optimal of 10.0 km, a 1.5 km excess, and the trip record carries the same two figures. The rider's claim that the trip ran 1.5 km longer than the route shown at booking is therefore supported by the platform's own trace.

Nothing on the driver's side reduces that excess, and the burden to point to something is the driver's under POL-RD-08. The only traffic advisory in the bundle is missing from the record (no payload, and as a MISSING artifact it can carry no fact and cannot support a POL-RD-03 closure excuse); the chat log holds a single rider message with no detour instruction and a null waypoint_hint, so POL-RD-04 is unavailable; and neither endpoint carries an amendment timestamp, so POL-RD-05 cannot run. The driver's counter-statement that he 'stayed on ordinary through roads and made no additional stop' identifies no artifact and no clause and, under POL-RD-08, is a general assertion that carries no weight.

The amount the rider contests is not a round number plucked from the air: it is exactly what POL-RD-02 produces. The fare breakdown shows a charged total of 19.39; the recomputation is base 3.80 + 0.75 x 10.0 km + 0.28 x 20 min, at the surge multiplier of 1.0 recorded on the fare breakdown, plus the 0.80 platform fee, giving 17.70; the difference is 1.69, rounded up to 1.70 payable. That is the figure the rider has claimed.

The rider does not overstate the record. The excess is 15.00% of the optimal distance, and POL-RD-01 requires the excess to exceed 20% of optimal as well as 0.8 km absolute, with both tests passing. The 1.5 km excess clears the absolute limb but not the percentage limb, so on the trace figures the deviation is not established, no refund is available under POL-RD-02, and the rider cannot on this evidence obtain the sum claimed. The rider makes no billing-integrity allegation: no gantry is charged (erp_gantries is empty) and the airport surcharge line is 0.00, so POL-RD-09(4) has nothing to bite on.

POL-RD-01 sets two cumulative establishment tests: the excess must be greater than 20% of optimal_distance_km AND greater than 0.8 km in absolute terms, and both must pass. Here the trace measures 11.5 km against a 10.0 km optimal route, an excess of 1.5 km which is only 15.00%. The percentage limb fails, so no deviation is established on this trip and the rider's claim falls at the gate before any refund arithmetic is reached.

The governing distance is the GPS trace figure of 11.5 km, which POL-RD-01 makes authoritative over the rounded trip_record convenience copy. The two fields agree at 11.5 km against the 10.0 km optimal route, so there is no hidden larger detour being suppressed by rounding: the excess is genuinely 1.5 km and no more.

There is no billing-integrity correction for the rider to fall back on under POL-RD-09(4), which is available whether or not a deviation exists. The fare_breakdown carries no ERP gantry lines at all (erp_gantries empty, tolls_erp 0.00), no airport surcharge (0.00), and the gps_trace passes no charge line that is missing a counterpart. No standalone refund issues on the pass-through limb.

The 1.5 km excess is measured on a clean trace, not a broken one. The GPS artifact covers 100% of the trip across 133 fixes with no gaps and a maximum inter-fix interval of 0.0 seconds, so it meets no impairment limb of POL-RD-07 and the threshold figure needs no independent corroboration. Whatever the excess is, it is reliably measured.

No repeat-deviation pattern exists to weigh against the driver on this trip. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 over completed_trips_90d of 610, a ratio of 0.00, well below both the 3-flag and the 0.05-ratio thresholds of POL-RD-06. The POL-RD-06 rider-favourable resolution, the full-refund uplift and the conduct referral are all unengaged, and every other counter on the profile is context only under POL-GEN-01.

No escalation trigger under POL-RD-10 fires. Trip identifier TRP-09112 matches across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown; the trace is unimpaired; pickup and dropoff timestamps are consistent with no reversal; and no charge line lacks a counterpart in the trace or trip record. The case is decidable on the present record and should be ruled, not held.

The correct outcome is NO_ACTION. Under POL-GEN-03 that value means the filing party's claim is not supported and the present payment state stands: fare_breakdown.payment_status is CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd is 0.00, so on this rider-filed dispute the charge remains exactly as it is and the rider recovers nothing.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: this dispute turns on whether the trip ran longer than the route shown at booking, and the answer is measured, not argued. The platform's own GPS trace (EV-GPS-09112) records 11.5 km against the booked optimal route of 10.0 km (EV-TRIP-09112), an excess of 1.5 km — 15.00% of the optimal distance. POL-RD-01 establishes a deviation only where the excess is greater than 20% of the optimal distance AND greater than 0.8 km in absolute terms, and both tests must pass. Here the 1.5 km excess clears the 0.8 km limb but fails the percentage limb (15.00% is below 20%), so no deviation is established on this trip and no distance refund is available under POL-RD-02. The rider's own advocate correctly concedes this gate; the 1.5 km figure the rider quotes is real, but it does not reach the threshold the policy sets. The rider's arithmetic (charged total 19.39 less a recomputed fare of 17.70 = 1.69) is correct in itself, but POL-RD-02 only runs once a deviation is established, so that sum does not become payable, and no amount is refunded.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
ruling.explanation_continued: The trace supporting the measurement is unimpaired: EV-GPS-09112 covers 100% of the trip with 133 fixes, no gaps and a maximum inter-fix interval of 0.0 s, so it meets no impairment limb (a)–(c) of POL-RD-07 and no corroboration question arises. The driver's statement that he stayed on ordinary through roads and made no additional stop, and the rider's in-app message that the trip looked a little longer, do not change the measurement — neither identifies a rider-requested detour nor an exculpatory traffic event. The traffic advisory artifact (EV-ADVIS-09112-01) carries no payload and can carry no fact, but since no deviation is established there is nothing for it to excuse. No billing-integrity correction applies under POL-RD-09(4): the fare breakdown carries no ERP gantry lines (tolls_erp 0.00) and no airport surcharge (0.00). No driver compensation arises under POL-RD-04: the distance charged (11.5 km) is not less than the 11.5 km the trace records, so the unbilled-shortfall limb is not met. No repeat-deviation pattern engages POL-RD-06 (deviation_flags_90d 0 over 610 completed trips in 90 days). No POL-RD-10 escalation trigger fires: trip_id TRP-09112 matches across the trip record, trace and fare breakdown, the trace is unimpaired, timestamps are consistent, and every charge line has a counterpart. Outcome: NO_ACTION — the filing party's claim is not supported by the evidence on the threshold test, and the present payment state (payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00) stands unchanged. The confidence is 0.95, the deciding facts being carried by artifacts at full weight (EV-GPS-09112 and EV-TRIP-09112).
